narrative:
The model determined that you have a 55% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and how long you have been employed. The requested loan term of 48 months was the biggest driver pushing the prediction toward denial. This duration is more than twice as long as the average 19 months seen among approved applicants, signaling higher risk to the bank. Your checking account status showing between 0 and 200 DM was the second strongest factor and also increased the likelihood of being classified as bad credit, especially since most approved applicants have no checking account or a higher balance. 

Your employment duration of 4 to 7 years worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. However, this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the impact of the longer loan term and checking account status.

To improve your chances on a future application, consider requesting a shorter loan period, building up your checking account balance before applying, or exploring smaller loan amounts. These changes would directly address the main reasons this application was turned down. (218 words)
